spec.name: Earnings drift v30
spec.notes: Post-earnings drift on the reported surprise.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.2, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 3.03 against 2.17 in research, a gap of -0.86.
The log holds 5 distinct specs; the best of 5 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.07, so the claimed 2.20 becomes 2.13 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.27 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.54).
Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.17 to 2.13 (change -0.04).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.17 to as low as 1.89 (as low as 2.14 at 25%).

verdict.opinion: The strategy's Sharpe ratio in the sealed period (3.03) is significantly higher than the research period (2.17), suggesting potential lookahead bias. This discrepancy indicates the strategy may not perform as claimed in live trading, warranting rejection.
